key_insight: The paper shows that a 2D chiral fluid has a nonstandard antisymmetric pressure term driven by a parity-breaking pseudo-scalar, and that this chiral pressure persists even in a homogeneous quiescent state.
engineering_relevance: This gives CFD and reduced-order models a new constitutive effect to capture when simulating micropolar or chiral fluids, especially systems with intrinsic rotation or rough-particle microstructure.
method: Derived the microscopic origin of the chiral pressure from the averaged pseudo-scalar in the fluid.
Connected the effect to rotational (vortex) viscosity in micropolar hydrodynamics.
Computed the kinetic value for rough disks to Gaussian order.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an analytical microscopic derivation and kinetic calculation, showing the chiral pressure and rotational viscosity survive at zeroth order in gradients in the steady Quiescent Chiral State.
watch_item: The result is specialized to 2D chiral fluids with rough-disk kinetics, so direct use in 3D or non-chiral flows may require re-derivation or calibration.
paper_title: Microscopic origin of the chiral pressure in a two-dimensional fluid
